note: Do not price this scenario as a lump sum off these rows. The steel rows can legitimately build a bespoke fabricated support frame and its cleats, brackets, base plates and connections once a weight take-off exists, but nearly all real NZ solar arrays use a proprietary rail kit rather than bespoke steel, so a bespoke-steel build-up will read high and should be flagged as an alternative, not the default. The design fee is web-researchable as an indicative percentage or hourly range for a chartered structural engineer but should be a named quote allowance for anything beyond a small residential array. The mounting kit is quote-only from the solar supplier. The perforated screen, cycle rack, emergency lighting, sprinkler, access control, carpet, aquarium, parking, dormitory and rooflight rows in this shortlist are irrelevant retrieval noise and are cited nowhere above.
title: Solar array mounting structural support

rows.role: Primary face rate - aluminium sheet wall cladding 1.6mm, measured m2 of cladding face; the base build-up item for the scenario.
rows.caveat: Unreviewed: not stated whether supply-only or supply-and-fix, and whether it is plain/coated sheet or a true composite (ACP) panel. Note this table contains TWO price bands for the same thicknesses (r6-r9 flat across all centres vs r2-r4 centre-varied) - the flat-priced band looks like a material/supply-only sub-table and the centre-varied band like a fixed rate. Reviewer must settle which band is installed work before use; do not mix bands.

rows.role: Thickness alternative (1.2mm) to the primary face rate for lighter sheet specification.
rows.caveat: Same band/convention question as r7; confirm gauge suits 10m-height wind loading before substituting.

rows.role: Thickness alternative (2mm) - upper-bound face rate where a heavier cassette panel is specified.
rows.caveat: Flat six-centre pricing again suggests supply/material convention; confirm before adding labour separately or double-counting fix.

rows.role: Cross-check / alternative band face rate (1.2mm, centre-varied) to test which band is installed work.
rows.caveat: Duplicate description to r6 at a materially lower price - one of the two bands must be discarded, not averaged.

rows.role: Subgirt/support component - top hat and intermediate top hat rails at 600mm crs (2.5 lm/m2), expressed per m2 of facade, used to price the cavity/subgirt layer behind the sheet.
rows.caveat: Row is drawn from the FC Exotec commercial facade build-up, so it is a component line within an aggregate system; confirm it is rail supply+fix only and that it is NOT already embedded in whichever aluminium sheet rate is adopted. Steel top hat vs aluminium subgirt is a material mismatch to flag.

rows.role: Exact duplicate of t41:r21 - use only to confirm the subgirt rate, never add both.
rows.caveat: Capture duplication across two tables; pick one instance.

rows.role: Standard flashing - base and cavity closure flashing to bottom of cladding, linear metre.
rows.caveat: Measured per m, not m2: needs a quantity assumption (lm of base per m2 of facade) to fold into the m2 scenario rate. Sized for 20/35mm timber cavity - confirm compatibility with a top-hat subgirt cavity depth.

rows.role: Colorsteel Maxx variant of the base/cavity closure flashing - specification alternative.
rows.caveat: Same rate as r2 despite differing description; duplicate risk - use one only. Colorsteel against aluminium raises a bimetallic-contact spec query for the designer.

rows.role: External corner flashing (90x90 behind cladding), linear metre, for standard corner detailing.
rows.caveat: Per m; requires corner-length allowance per m2. 'Behind cladding' convention means the visible aluminium corner trim/extrusion may still be unpriced.

rows.role: Internal corner flashing, linear metre, completes standard flashing set.
rows.caveat: Per m; quantity assumption required. Timber-cladding flashing family - confirm acceptable on a rainscreen sheet system.

rows.role: Vertical control joint back flashing, linear metre - needed where sheet runs are broken at movement joints on a 10m elevation.
rows.caveat: Per m; only applies if control joints are detailed. Do not add by default.

rows.role: Aggregate sanity-check only - complete proprietary facade panel system total per m2, used as an upper-bound reasonableness test on the assembled rate.
rows.caveat: AGGREGATE: this line already contains panel + top hat + fixings + accessories, so it double-counts t41:r21 and the face rate. Never add it to component rows. Note two conflicting 'system total' values exist (r33 and r17) - different area bands or spec, unresolved.

missing: Nothing that blocks a build. The scenario's own scope permits sheet cladding, and face area, subgirt and standard flashings are all represented. Unpriced by design and to be stated as exclusions: access/scaffolding to 10m, proprietary ACP cassette fabrication/routing and folded returns, PE vs FR (fire-rated) core selection, and any design/producer-statement or specific-engineering-design input for a rainscreen over 10m.
search_capture_for: If the reviewer rejects the plain-sheet substitution, search the capture for proprietary ACP trade names (Alucobond, Vitrabond, Alpolic, Larson, Symonite) under Metalwork or Proprietary Cladding Systems; also search for 'aluminium subgirt' / 'top hat' rails under Metalwork rather than the FC Exotec table, and for the Metalwork/Aluminium Sheet Cladding table header note that distinguishes the two price bands (supply vs fixed). Scaffolding rates sit in Preliminaries/Scaffolding if access must be carried.
note: Build as: adopted face rate (one band only) + subgirt m2 + flashings converted from lm to an m2 allowance using measured corner/base/joint lengths. The two duplicated price bands in the aluminium sheet table and the duplicated top hat and system-total rows are the main capture hazards - each pair must be resolved to a single line. Do not blend component rows with any 'system total' row. Six-centre spread is nil on several rows (flat national pricing), which itself signals a supply-only convention and should be confirmed before regional adjustment is applied.
title: Aluminium composite panel cladding

rows.role: Only marginally relevant row: alterations/disconnection or removal of an existing switchboard or distribution board, usable as the strip-out/make-safe component if the existing board is replaced rather than retro-braced.
rows.caveat: Sits in Demolition and Alterations / Work in Connection With Services, so it is almost certainly disconnect-and-remove (or isolate/reconnect) labour only - it is not supply, not installation, and carries no board, busbar or protective device content. Reviewer must confirm whether the rate covers electrician attendance, isolation and certification, and whether it assumes a small DB rather than a main switchboard (no size/rating band stated). Unit 'each' per board must be confirmed. Do not use it as a proxy for any part of the fault-rating work.

missing: Everything that makes up the scenario: (a) a fault level / short-circuit and protection coordination study to AS/NZS 3000 and AS 3851 - this is consulting electrical engineer time, not measured work; (b) switchboard manufacturer's shop work to uprate busbar bracing / replace busbar chamber to a higher kA withstand on an existing Form-rated board, including type-test evidence and re-labelling; (c) supply and installation of correctly rated MCBs/MCCBs/ACBs, cascade/energy-let-through matched devices, and main switch/incomer; (d) network company confirmation of prospective fault current at the point of supply; (e) outage/after-hours and temporary supply costs while the board is de-energised. Items (a), (b) and (d) are not rates QV publishes.
search_capture_for: Electrical Services / Mains and Submains, Switchboards, Distribution Boards, Main Switchboard, Circuit Protection - search the capture for 'switchboard', 'distribution board', 'circuit breaker', 'MCB', 'MCCB', 'RCD', 'main switch', 'busbar', 'submain' and any 'Electrical' section rates per board or per pole/way, plus 'Preliminaries / After hours work' or 'out of hours' loading and 'temporary electrical supply'. If QV carries a per-way DB rate and per-pole breaker rates, the device replacement element can be partly measured, but the bracing uprate and the study still cannot.
note: The scenario is engineering assessment plus a proprietary switchboard modification, not a catalogue-measurable build-up, so it cannot be priced from this shortlist at any confidence. Fault level assessment fees are web-researchable as an indicative consultant hourly/lump-sum range (typically scoped per board), but the network operator's prospective fault current data must be requested from the lines company. The busbar bracing uprate and any Form-segregation or type-test re-verification are quote-only from the original switchboard manufacturer or an accredited assembler, because the permissible modification depends on the board's type-test certificate. Protection device supply, if QV rates surface, should be checked for supply-only versus supply-and-fix and for whether the device rating band (frame size, kA breaking capacity) matches; a generic 'circuit breaker each' rate captured at domestic 6kA will badly under-price a 50kA-rated commercial device. Also confirm that any aggregate 'switchboard each' rate found does not already include its own protective devices before adding breakers separately, or the devices will be double-counted. No price has been derived here.
title: Switchboard fault rating and protection

rows.role: Only directly relevant row: covers the existing-board side of the works - disconnection/removal (or alteration) of a switchboard or distribution board where the existing board is stripped out or made safe prior to the PV connection.
rows.caveat: Sits in Demolition and Alterations / Work in Connection With Services, so it is almost certainly a disconnect-and-remove (or make-safe) labour rate, NOT supply or install of a new board and NOT an 'upgrade' of a live board. Unit 'each' - confirm whether it is per board regardless of size/way count, whether isolation, temporary supply, certification and disposal are included, and whether it assumes a registered electrician's attendance or is a builder's attendance rate. Cannot be reused as a proxy for a new solar DB.

missing: Everything on the supply/install side: new dedicated solar distribution board (supply and fix, ways/rating), solar supply main switch / AC isolator and lockable isolation at the board, MCB/RCBO circuit protection, sub-main and consumer-mains cabling and terminations from inverter to board, labelling/signage to AS/NZS 4777 and 3000, upgrade/extension of the existing MSB or DB (added ways, new main switch, tails), and electrician test, certification (CoC/ESC) and inverter commissioning. Also outside measured work: the lines-company/distributor connection application and ICP/meter change fees and any retailer export-meter charge.
search_capture_for: Electrical Services section tables - 'Switchboards', 'Distribution Boards' (supply and install, by number of ways / amperage), 'Main Switchboard', 'Circuit breakers / MCB / RCD / RCBO', 'Isolating switch / isolator', 'Sub-mains and consumer mains cable (per m, by size)', 'Cable tray/conduit', 'Testing and commissioning' or 'Connect, test and commission' rows within Electrical Services rather than Security Systems; also any 'Photovoltaic / Solar' or 'Renewable energy' sub-section under Electrical Services or Specialist Services.
note: The shortlist is dominated by irrelevant retrieval noise (structural steel 'connection plates/brackets', plaster/cladding 'board' matches, intruder-alarm panel, landscaping) - these matched on the words 'connection' and 'board' only and must not be used. The intruder-alarm rows (ac5fef...:t38:r1, :t38:r8) are alarm-specific and are not a legitimate proxy for a solar board or its commissioning. Once the Electrical Services board/isolator/sub-main rows are surfaced the scenario is buildable from QV, except the distributor/retailer connection and metering fees, which QV does not publish - those are web-researchable from the local lines company and retailer price lists, with inverter and PV-specific accessory pricing quote-only.
title: Solar connection switchboard works

rows.role: Closest priced proxy for the two-coat acrylic paint system on plastered/concrete substrate (seal + 2 coats), applied per m2 of coated area
rows.caveat: Row sits under Wall Finishes / Wall Linings and Finishes, i.e. an internal lining context. Reviewer must confirm whether the sealer/paint specification, prep allowance and coverage are valid for an exterior-grade system, and whether any exterior prep (water blast, fungicidal wash, making good) is included or must be added separately. No access/height loading included.

rows.role: Priced proxy for the coated-steel-panel portion of the facade — acrylic etch primer plus two coats, per m2
rows.caveat: Published under Metal Roofing; reviewer must confirm it transfers to vertical steel wall/facade panels (girth vs plan area measurement, profile development factor) and whether prep of factory-coated or galvanised panel (degrease/etch) is inside the rate. Assume applied-only, no scaffolding.

rows.role: Alternative/comparator if the specified system is a high-build exterior coating rather than conventional two-coat paint
rows.caveat: Flexitrowel is a trowel-applied high-build styrene acrylic with scratch finish — a different product class and a much higher rate than a two-coat paint. Do not use as the base two-coat rate; use only if the spec is genuinely high-build. Confirm whether substrate prep and glaze/topcoat are included and whether it is single-application or a system.

rows.role: Reference for site-applied topcoat to structural steel elements within the facade
rows.caveat: No six-centre prices captured (nulls) — cannot be used to build a number. Also one coat only, and the description expressly excludes hot dip galvanised surfaces which need degrease/etch/prime first.

rows.role: Indicative only — soffit work measured to the underside of timber joists, useful for the soffit geometry/measurement convention
rows.caveat: This is cement plaster to soffit, i.e. a rendering trade item, not a coating. It would double-count if added to a coating rate applied over the same soffit. Use for measurement logic only, not as a coating price.

missing: A dedicated exterior painting section: preparation (water blast / fungicidal wash / make good) and seal-plus-two-coats acrylic to exterior plastered, render, concrete and fibre-cement surfaces, plus the matching exterior soffit/eaves painting rate. Also missing the access component — scaffolding or EWP to 10m — which the scenario says is to be included in the m2 rate. The plaster/cladding system rows in this shortlist (Thermaclad, Rockcote, ExoTec, Easylap) are full cladding build-ups and would grossly double-count if used as a coating rate.
search_capture_for: Painting & Specialist Finishes — 'Walls, Exterior' and 'Soffits/Eaves, Exterior' sub-tables: 'Prepare and two coats acrylic, exterior', 'Water blast / prepare existing exterior surfaces', 'Sealer to plaster/concrete, exterior'; also Preliminaries & General — 'Scaffolding' (m2 of elevation, per week hire, erect/dismantle) and 'Elevated Work Platform / scissor lift hire'; and Structural Steelwork — 'Steelwork Surface Treatments' rows with populated six-centre pricing.
note: Buildable coating rates exist in the capture but this shortlist surfaced mostly cladding-system and floor-coating rows. Several of the most relevant rows (steel topcoat, Rockcote render systems, residential all-up $/m2 rows) have null pricing and cannot be cited as numbers. Flag that any all-up residential $/m2 rows (3b624bfa…) are building-cost-per-floor-area indices, not coating rates. Scaffolding is measured work QV publishes, so this is needs_more_qv rather than needs_outside; if the capture has no scaffolding table, revert to a hire quote.
title: Facade and soffit coating

rows.role: Glass component for a non-rated / acoustic-rated vision panel - 12.38mm clear laminate, applied to the panel area (300x900 = 0.27 m²)
rows.caveat: Sits under 'Glazing: Other' at the same $250/m² as the glazed-partition row ffb...:t11:r1, so it is almost certainly the same published rate duplicated - use one only, never both. Unreviewed whether it is supply-only glass or supply+install into partition framing (if install is included it double-counts the bead/fixing rows below). Small-pane minimum charge almost certainly applies: 0.27 m² x rate will under-price a cut-to-size vision pane; reviewer must settle a minimum-pane allowance. Not a fire-rated product.

rows.role: Alternative glass component where an STC 39 acoustic vision panel is specified - 12.76mm acoustic laminate
rows.caveat: Duplicate of ffb...:t11:r2 at the same $320/m²; pick one. Same supply-only vs supply-and-fix ambiguity and same small-pane minimum problem. STC rating is acoustic, not a fire rating - it does not answer the scenario's 'glass to rating' if that means FRR.

rows.role: Cross-check source for the 12.38mm laminate glass rate (glazed partitions section)
rows.caveat: Same description and price as 2dc5...:t24:r17 - treat as the same rate, not an additional item. Being a partition rate it may include framing/install content that is not applicable to a door leaf aperture.

rows.role: Cross-check source for the 12.76mm acoustic glass rate
rows.caveat: Duplicate of 2dc5...:t24:r18; do not add both.

rows.role: Glazing bead to both faces of the aperture - 18x12x6mm RP clears H3.1, measured on panel perimeter (approx 2.4 lin m per face, 4.8 m both faces)
rows.caveat: Unit convention unconfirmed: is $22.70/m supply-and-fix or supply-only timber? If supply-only, the fixing row t3:r10 must be added; if fix is already in, adding r10 double-counts. H3.1 treated exterior bead is likely over-spec for an internal door - a clears/FJ interior profile may be the correct pick. Bead depth must suit 12.38-12.76mm glass; a 6mm rebate bead will not hold laminate of this thickness.

rows.role: Alternative deeper bead (30x10x6mm RP clears) where the thicker laminate/acoustic pane needs a larger rebate cover
rows.caveat: Same supply-only vs fixed ambiguity; choose one bead profile only, do not stack r5, r6, r7, r8, r2 and r3 together.

rows.role: Fixing of beads with brass screws and cups, per lin m of bead
rows.caveat: Only add if the chosen bead row is confirmed supply-only. Brass screws and cups is a finish-joinery convention; a painted commercial door may use pins and stopping instead, so the reviewer should confirm the fixing method matches the specification.

missing: The core labour operation is absent: cutting/forming the aperture in a manufactured door leaf (marking out, cutting through both faces, lipping or blocking the exposed core edge, making good and preparing for beads). None of the shortlisted rows measure that. Also absent is fire-rated glass and rated glazing componentry (e.g. Pyrostop/Pyran type insulated or integrity glass, intumescent glazing tape/seals, rated bead system and the rated-door-set certification/relabelling that a site-cut vision panel triggers). The shortlisted glass rows are acoustic/laminate only. No door leaf row here corresponds to a plain flush leaf being modified - the 1/2/8-light and entrance door rows are complete factory door sets, so using them would double-count the leaf. Note also the glass rows are m² with no small-pane minimum, while the scenario is a 0.27 m² pane.
search_capture_for: Search the capture for: (1) Doors / Doors, Timber, Flush or Solid Core sub-sections for 'vision panel', 'glazed lite', 'view panel', 'aperture' or 'extra over for glazing to door'; (2) Glazing section for 'fire rated glazing', 'Pyrostop', 'Pyran', 'Pyroshield', 'wired glass', '-/30/30', '-/60/60'; (3) 'intumescent' seals/glazing tape under Doors hardware or Fire Protection / Passive Fire Stopping; (4) Carpentry or Joinery labour constants / hourly rates (carpenter, joiner) to build up the cut-and-frame operation if no composite exists; (5) 'fire door' rows to see whether QV publishes an extra-over for a vision panel in a rated leaf.
note: Only if the capture has no fire-rated vision panel item does this become needs_outside: FRR glass supply and, critically, the fire-door manufacturer's approval/relabelling for a site-cut aperture in a rated leaf are quote-only (door manufacturer or IANZ-certified installer) - a site-cut panel voids the leaf's certification unless done to the manufacturer's tested detail. Product-only pricing for rated glass is partly web-researchable from NZ glazing suppliers, but the certification is not. For a non-rated leaf, this scenario is buildable once a cut-aperture labour row or joinery labour rate surfaces. Six-centre spread: bead, glass and fixing rows are all flat nationally, so no regional factor falls out of these rows - the reviewer should confirm whether the flat rate is a genuine national rate or an uncaptured centre variation.
title: Glazed vision panel to door

rows.role: Re-erect temporary site fence in its new alignment (labour to install, per m of fence line).
rows.caveat: Unit convention unconfirmed - $2.90/m is identical to the hire and dismantle rows, which suggests either a per m per period hire component or a capture artefact. Reviewer must confirm this is a one-off install labour rate and whether panels/feet/couplers are supply-inclusive or hire-only.

rows.role: Take down the existing fence line before relocation (a relocation = dismantle + re-install).
rows.caveat: Confirm it is not already embedded in the hire-period rows (t4:r8/r9/r10); if the period rates are all-in supply+install+dismantle, pricing r3+r4 on top double-counts.

rows.role: Ongoing hire of the relocated fence line for the balance of the civil contract (200m+, 6-12 months band).
rows.caveat: Aggregate-risk row: unclear whether the rate is per m per week, per m per month, or per m for the whole stated duration, and whether it already includes install/dismantle. Must be resolved before combining with r3/r4.

rows.role: Alternative hire band if the reconfigured compound fence line falls in the 50-200m / 6-9 month range.
rows.caveat: Same unit-period ambiguity as r10; pick one band only, do not add bands together.

rows.role: Delivery of additional fence panels from hire depot for the reconfigured compound.
rows.caveat: Per-load 'each' - confirm whether one charge covers a full truckload and how many loads the fence length requires; a purely internal relocation may incur no depot transport at all.

rows.role: Return of surplus fence panels to depot after reconfiguration.
rows.caveat: Only applies if panel count reduces; otherwise omit. Same 'per load vs per event' ambiguity as r5.

rows.role: Barrier mesh to delineate relocated stockpile and material storage areas.
rows.caveat: Explicitly excludes supports - waratahs/star pickets must be priced separately and are not in this shortlist.

rows.role: Danger tape for short-term demarcation during the compound move.
rows.caveat: Supply-only assumption; no fixing/support included.

rows.role: Replacement/relocated 'Construction Keep Out' signage on the new fence line.
rows.caveat: Confirm supply-only vs supply-and-fix; existing signs may simply be re-hung at nil material cost.

rows.role: Site hazard signage re-posted at the reconfigured compound entry.
rows.caveat: Supply vs supply-and-fix unconfirmed; avoid double-counting with r2/r3 if one sign suite is being reused.

rows.role: Site danger signage at the relocated gate.
rows.caveat: Same supply/fix ambiguity; quantity driven by number of new access points, not measured here.

rows.role: Shifting existing stockpiled material to the new stockpile location (cut and remove to stockpile within 500m).
rows.caveat: Written as excavation-to-stockpile, not re-handle of an existing loose stockpile - loosening/loading of already-won material may be cheaper or dearer. Confirm whether it includes load, cart and tip, and confirm m3 is bank or loose measure.

rows.role: Load and cart of unsuitable/surplus material out of the footprint being reconfigured.
rows.caveat: Destination is 'to stockpile' not to tip - disposal off site is not covered. Confirm haul distance assumption and measure basis.

rows.role: Crane driver travel time if a mobile crane is used to lift sheds/containers to the new compound position.
rows.caveat: This is only the driver's transport component - the crane hire itself, mobilisation and minimum-hire charge are not in this shortlist, so it cannot be used alone.

missing: The shed/site-accommodation half of the scenario. Nothing in the shortlist prices site office, lunchroom, ablution or lockable container hire, nor the shift/relocation event for those units (uplift, transport within or to site, re-levelling on bearers, re-connection of temporary power/water/data). The mobile crane hire rate itself (hourly rate, mobilisation, minimum hire) is also absent - only the driver transport line surfaced. The 'site establishment cost, stud welding contractor' rows (52d4a...:t10:r8 and 15a23...:t5:r33) are trade-specific establishment lump sums for a stud welding subcontractor and are not transferable to general compound relocation; note also that 15a23...:t5:r33 has a null unit and appears to be a duplicate of the same item.
search_capture_for: Preliminaries section: 'Site Accommodation', 'Site Huts', 'Site Offices', 'Lunchroom', 'Ablutions / portable toilet hire', 'Container hire', 'Storage container', 'Cabin delivery / uplift', 'Relocate on site'; also the full 'Preliminaries / Mobile Crane Hire' table (253b838a...:t9 rows other than r21) for crane hourly rates, mobilisation and minimum hire; and 'Temporary Services' for disconnect/reconnect of temporary power and water to relocated sheds.
note: Fencing, delineation, signage and stockpile re-handle can all be built from this shortlist once the fence rate unit convention is settled, but a compound relocation sum is not credible without shed/container shift and craneage rates. Flag for the reviewer that the four fence rows at $2.90/m (install, dismantle, civil hire, and the two 3.50 hire bands) are suspiciously uniform and must be checked against the source table headings before any are stacked. All rates are the same in all three centres for the fence, crane-transport and stud-welding rows, i.e. no regional loading - confirm this is QV's convention and not a capture fill-down.
title: Site establishment and compound relocation
